8

Trap ’Em

An 8-Ball game of offense & defense

Every shot is offense. Every shot is defense.

Trap ’Em is a strategic variation of 8-Ball where every player gets exactly ONE shot per inning.
You’re not just trying to pocket your own ball — you’re trying to play safe against your opponent.

How to play

Played under the current CSI Official Rules for 8-Ball, with a few Trap ’Em specific rules:

Each player gets exactly ONE shot per inning, regardless of the result of that shot.

Like baseball, an inning is one turn for each player. In Trap ’Em every turn is a single shot, so an inning is one shot each.

Exceptions: a ball legally pocketed on the break earns one more shot, and after a non-scratch foul your opponent may make you shoot again.

Pocket a legal ball?Your turn is over.
Miss?Your turn is over.
Play a safety?Your turn is over.
Scratch or cue ball off the table?Your turn is over, and your opponent gets ball in hand.
Bad hit, no rail, or other foul?Your turn is over. Your opponent may shoot it as it lies or make you shoot again.

Players alternate innings until the game is won.

Rules

1The break

If the breaker legally pockets a ball on the break, they get one more shot to try to establish their group.
After that shot, the turn passes. If nothing is pocketed, the turn passes right away.

2After the break

The table is open. To claim a group, call the ball and pocket it legally.
This(and the 8-ball) is the only time you need to call your shot.
A ball that drops without a call does not set the groups, and the table stays open.

38-ball on the break

Handled the same as CSI 8-Ball.

4When to call your shot

Only two shots need a call: any shot at the 8-ball, and a shot on an open table that you want to set your group.
Pocketing the 8 without calling it, or in a pocket you didn’t call, loses the game.
Once groups are set, no other calls are needed except for the 8-ball.

5Ball in hand: cue ball scratched or off the table

Pocketing the cue ball or driving it off the table gives the opponent ball in hand. Ball in hand does not add an extra shot.
Three fouls in a row also gives ball in hand (rule 7).
All other fouls give the opponent the choice in rule 6.
CSI loss-of-game fouls still apply.

6Other fouls: opponent’s option

Any foul other than a cue-ball scratch or off table is not ball in hand.
The opponent may shoot the table as it lies, or make the shooter shoot again from where the balls stopped.
The cue ball must first hit a ball of the shooter’s group, or the 8 once their group is cleared (on an open table, any ball except the 8).
After that contact, a ball must be pocketed or some ball must hit a rail.
A shoot-again shot follows the same rules, so if it is also a foul, the opponent chooses again.
Fouls that lose the game under CSI 8-ball rules still lose.

7Three fouls in a row

Like the 10-Ball three-foul rule, but the penalty is ball in hand instead of loss of game.
If the same player fouls on three of their own shots in a row, including shoot-again shots, the opponent gets ball in hand.
The opponent must tell the player when they are on two fouls.
Without that warning, the third foul does not count toward the rule.
A legal shot by that player resets the count.

8Pocketing your opponent’s ball

On a legal shot it is not a foul. The ball stays down, and your turn is over like any other shot.

9Stalemate

If neither player can make progress, the CSI stalemate rule applies: re-rack, and the original breaker breaks again.

The strategy

In regular 8-Ball, making a ball lets you keep shooting, so position play is about leaving yourself a shot.
In Trap ’Em, your opponent comes to the table after every shot.

Can I make my ball & get position?

Can I make my ball and leave my opponent trapped?

  • Pocket a ball while hiding the cue ball.
  • Use your remaining balls as blockers.
  • Tie up your opponent’s balls.
  • Avoid opening their problem areas.
  • Sometimes the best ball to make isn’t the easiest one.
  • Sometimes a ball is worth more on the table than in a pocket.

Winning the game

Same as standard 8-Ball: legally pocket your group, then legally pocket the 8-ball.

You lose the game if you:
  • Pocket the 8 before your group is cleared (except on the break).
  • Pocket the 8 without calling it, or in a pocket you didn’t call.
  • Scratch or foul on the shot that pockets the 8.
  • Drive the 8 off the table.

Everything not covered above follows CSI 8-Ball rules.
